critics.name: spec
critics.intent: Does the diff do what the ticket and the brief ask, and does it do it correctly: missing or partial requirements, scope creep, and wrong behavior (false cache hits, exit codes, missed inputs, edge cases). It runs on every change.

critics.name: standards
critics.intent: Does the diff follow the documented repo rules (the root AGENTS.md, the AGENTS.md of each app, and lessons-learned) and the smell baseline of the code-review skill. It runs on every change.

critics.name: simplicity
critics.intent: Is each part of the diff essential for the job, or accidental machinery: unused options, wrappers, fields and modes, and leftover analogue design. Spec-match is not a defense. It runs on every change.

critics.name: security
critics.intent: Trust surfaces. They are credentials and tokens, auth and organization isolation, and OIDC and IAM trust. They are CI workflow trust: permissions, secrets, environments, triggers and third-party actions. They are sandboxes and egress, and model routing to an outside provider. They are code that runs at install, at check listing or at check discovery: dependency scripts, bin entries and git dependencies. They are data that leaves to a public artifact or an outside provider. A change that touches none of these is not a reason to run it. A workflow or package edit that does not change its trust is not a reason either.
notApplicable: no trust surface: the diff touches no credential, auth, CI workflow, IAM or infrastructure, install or discovery path, sandbox or egress, model routing, and no data that leaves to a public artifact or an outside provider
